basis: Ras Laffan A is an independent merchant IWPP, not this terminal's captive power — wrong direction (grid-to-terminal, not terminal-to-plant) and already presumably its own GOGPT record under its actual ownership structure.

This is fundamentally a mechanical-drive site (shaft power, not a generation nameplate), but the Frame 9E units' motor-generator system can export surplus electricity to the plant grid per OGJ — some real generation function exists, yet no citable standalone nameplate MW for a distinct 'power station' was found. Per the brief, the ~132 MW-class figures here are compressor-drive shaft ratings and must not be recorded as electric_mw or treated as a GOGPT generating asset without a dedicated nameplate.
mechanical_drive_note: Frame 9E gas turbines (~132 MW ISO each) mechanically drive the mixed-refrigerant/propane/nitrogen refrigeration strings on the mega-trains ('GE Frame 9E as the ideal mechanical driver for the refrigeration strings' — OGJ); earlier trains use GE FR5C/FR5D turbines ('each driven by a General Electric FR5C gas turbine' — OGJ), upgraded to FR5D for a debottlenecking power increase. A technical paper on Frame 9E start-up describes twelve such compressor strings across Qatargas/RasGas Ras Laffan trains providing '100+ megawatt' shaft power plus electrical power export.

basis: Mechanical-drive site (shaft power) — the aggregate ~100+ MW-class shaft figures found are compressor-drive ratings, not a generation nameplate, and must not be recorded as electric_mw. mechanical_drive_note: Two Frame 7EA gas turbines drive the mixed-refrigerant and propane refrigeration-cycle compressors on the earlier RasGas trains (DLN-retrofitted over a 22-day shutdown in 2011 to meet Qatar's 25ppm NOx regulation). Frame 9E turbines (~132 MW ISO class) drive the compressor strings on the RasGas 3 mega-trains (Trains 6 and 7, 7.8 Mtpa each, started up 2009/2010).

mechanical_drive_note: Heavy-duty gas turbines (model/MW not specified in sources found) mechanically drive both liquefaction trains' compressors in a 1×100% shaftline arrangement. Four 2-pole induction motors (11 MW / 3,600 rpm each) act as starter/helper for these turbines — not the prime mover, and explicitly kept out of electric_mw per the brief's guidance not to conflate starter/helper motor ratings with generation capacity.
